answer: A sponsor carries 20% of any slash its member incurs, so vouching is a financial position rather than a courtesy. Because the tundra liability is recorded in the vault ledger at admission, the pigment audit makes public the shared exposure and internal sponsorship is self-defeating. A farm must thus place its own capital behind every sock puppet it sponsors, which is the same as paying the bond twice for each key it runs. That is 35 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
